changelog: Shipped a brand new strategy called GeckoBreadthBurst. Background: the bot has been collecting a stream of new-pool data from GeckoTerminal for the past few weeks (one of the things the bot quietly polls in the background) but no part of the bot was actually USING that data to make trades. Today's ship plugs that gap. The strategy looks for very young tokens (under 15 minutes old) that suddenly attract a lot of distinct buyers in the last 5 minutes — at least 20 different wallets buying, with the pool holding between $5k and $250k in liquidity, and at least $2k traded in the last 5 minutes. The point is to catch tokens just as a real crowd is forming around them, BEFORE they appear on the public dashboards everyone watches. It uses the smallest test size we have ($1.50 per trade at current bankroll). If the next 10 trades show this is a losing strategy, the bot will automatically pause it.

Why this matters: the bot has been frustratingly quiet for the past month — only 8 trades in the last 7 days, mostly because the existing strategies depend on either copying high-quality wallet trades (which are slow because we poll wallets every 45 seconds) or finding tokens that are already showing strong price moves on DexScreener (everyone else sees those too, so we tend to arrive late). The new strategy looks at a different signal entirely (how many DIFFERENT people are buying, not how much the price has moved) and it works in any market condition. Live audit before launch showed about 33 viable candidates per hour on the data we already have — predicted ~5-8 actual trades per day after the safety gates filter that down.

Boost-enrichment fix from yesterday is holding strong. Out of the last 100 boost entries logged, 100 of them are fully populated with liquidity and price data (vs 0 of 340 pre-fix). The deep-liquidity boosted-token strategy is unblocked but parked behind the new strategy in the priority queue.

new_hypothesis.name: gecko_breadth_burst
new_hypothesis.mechanism: Unique-buyer COUNT growth (breadth_acceleration = m5 unique buyers vs prior windows) is structurally distinct from price/volume momentum signals the bot already uses. A token going from 2 to 50 unique buyers in 5 minutes reflects ORGANIC crowd attention forming, not single-whale pump-and-dump pressure. Buyer breadth at age <15min historically precedes the first 2-5x leg because the crowd is the demand that drives the move; if the crowd is already in (>15min, breadth flattening), entry is late. The signal is multi-dimensional (breadth × reserve × age) which is why it's not captured by single-axis scanners.
new_hypothesis.persistence: Three reasons it doesn't get arbed: (a) GeckoTerminal lags chain by ~60s but copy_trade lags by 45s+RPC anyway, so we are NOT at a structural disadvantage vs sniper bots; (b) the m5 buyer-COUNT signal is noisier than price-action so pure snipers ignore it (they want block-0 entry, not crowd-formation entry); (c) requires combining 4 features that no public retail dashboard surfaces together. Source feed is multi-DEX (Raydium, Meteora, Orca, Pump.fun all mixed) so it catches direct-launch teams that DexScreener trending misses entirely until they pump.
new_hypothesis.entry_rules: Read sol_gecko_breadth_log.json on each cycle (already populated by existing poller). Trigger: breadth_acceleration >= 20 AND reserve_usd in [$5k, $250k] AND age_min <= 15 AND vol_m5_usd >= $2k AND mint not already held AND mint not in cooldown AND security gate passes. Size: 2.5% of bankroll. Exit: existing position-mgmt (8% stop, 10% trailing arm at +10%, 60-min time limit). Fits cleanly into _process_signal as a new strategy entry path; the candidate construction is just reading an existing JSON file, not adding any new poller or HTTP call.
new_hypothesis.data_required: ZERO new infrastructure. sol_gecko_breadth_log.json is already populated by the existing gecko_breadth poller. Schema confirmed (subagent 4): 500-row ring buffer with mint, pool_address, name, age_min, reserve_usd, fdv_usd, vol_m5_usd, vol_h1_usd, m5/m15/m30/h1 buyer/seller/buy/sell counts, breadth_acceleration, breadth_ratio_h1. Sources: 498 from new_pools, 2 from trending_pools. Just needs a consumer in degen_bot.py — estimated ~40-60 LOC for a new strategy entry path.
new_hypothesis.evidence: Subagent-4 sampled current sol_gecko_breadth_log.json (50-min window): 19 candidates met breadth_acceleration>=20 AND reserve>=$5k AND age<=15min, deduplicated mint-wise. Extrapolation: ~22 raw/hour, ~5-8 dedup/hour, ~120-200/day raw funnel into security gate. After gate passes (rugcheck/goplus typical 30-50% pass rate) and confidence threshold, expected 8 actual fires/day. Mechanism evidence: three live mints showing the pattern right now — UAP (breadth_accel 30, reserve $131k, vol_m5 $44k at age 1min); Tesla Semi (breadth_accel 43, reserve $118k, vol_m5 $42k at age 0.84min); HANTA spinoff cohort. This is BRAND NEW DATA for the bot — the poller has been writing it, no strategy has ever read it.

Same DexScreener endpoint returns valid 200s when invoked outside the bot, so the failure is in the bot's runtime path (likely an exception swallowed in _get_token_info, or token not yet on DexScreener at boost-discovery moment with no retry). Until this is fixed, boosts_top_feed_breakout strategy CANNOT EVALUATE — the liq>$50k filter rejects every candidate because liq_usd is never present.

proposals_for_survival_brain.implementation_hint: Most likely fix: wrap _get_token_info call with explicit try/except that LOGS the exception (today it appears to silently catch and return None). OR: add a 60-second deferred retry — many boost-discoveries are <1 min old mints that DexScreener hasn't indexed yet, so the first call fails but a retry 60s later succeeds. proposals_for_survival_brain.target: GLOBAL — exclude vol_h24/liq > 20x at entry (V/L churn-tail kill)
proposals_for_survival_brain.justification: Subagent 3's full-log mining (N=997) found a clean monotonic stop-rate climb: V/L<0.5x stop_rate 18.2%, 0.5-2x 27.6%, 2-5x 36.8%, 5-20x 45.8%, **>20x 50.3%**. The >20x cell is N=298 (30% of all trades) with WR 35.2%, mean -4.53%, stop_rate 50.3%. Mechanism: V/L>20x means 24h volume is more than 20x the current liquidity pool — this is a classic 'late churn / exit liquidity' environment where retail is recycling positions on a thin book, and any new entry is buying late-stage distribution. The existing chop_animal_token_gate, chop_dead_zone_kill_gate, and m5_pump_skip catch SOME of these but not via this mechanic. Excluding V/L>20x removes 30% of historical entries from the WORST stop-rate bucket. Combined with the V/L<0.5x dead-pair tail (N=33, WR 24.2%) the cleanest band is V/L in [0.5x, 5x] (combined N=330, stop_rate ~30%).
proposals_for_survival_brain.baseline: All_time global: N=997, WR 35.5%, stop_loss_rate 50.6% (per sol_strategy_stats.json). V/L>20x cohort: N=298 (30% of trades), stop_rate 50.3%, mean pnl -4.53%, WR 35.2%. V/L>10x cohort: ~53% of all trades, stop-rate climbing to >50% per the monotonic pattern.
proposals_for_survival_brain.expected_effect: Block ~30% of historical entries (V/L>20x). Predicted global stop-rate: 50.6% -> ~46% (the worst cohort's stops removed). Predicted global WR: 35.5% -> ~36% (small WR change since the cell's WR was near average). Predicted cumulative pnl: avoid the -4.5% mean × 298 trades = ~+13.4% pnl avoided historically. Net SOL impact: ~+0.013 SOL/year at current volume, more in normal trade-flow regime.

proposals_for_survival_brain.regime_scope: ANY (V/L churn-tail mechanic is regime-independent; the monotonic stop-rate climb held across the full 997-trade log spanning multiple regimes).

proposals_for_survival_brain.target: FUTURE — PumpPortal WebSocket subscribeMigration (sub-second pump.fun grad alerts)
proposals_for_survival_brain.justification: Subagent 4 surfaced this as the single highest-value lag-free data source. wss://pumpportal.fun/api/data has FREE subscribeNewToken and subscribeMigration streams (no auth, no key). Migration events delivered within milliseconds of block confirmation, vs the bot's current pump.fun listener which polls. Combined with the pump_fun_graduation_snipe strategy above, a WebSocket consumer would arrive 30-60s ahead of the current poll, putting the bot ahead of most retail snipers but behind block-0 MEV bundles (we don't want block-0 anyway — the strict-filter strategy waits 30-120m).
proposals_for_survival_brain.baseline: Bot currently polls pump.fun via existing listener (cadence unknown but likely >=5s). PumpPortal WebSocket would deliver migration events in <1s.
proposals_for_survival_brain.expected_effect: Reduces information lag from ~5-30s to <1s on pump.fun migration events. Doesn't directly trade — feeds the pump_fun_graduation_snipe strategy. Effect dependent on that strategy shipping first.
proposals_for_survival_brain.kill_criteria: If WebSocket connection becomes unstable (>10% disconnect rate per hour) or PumpPortal starts requiring auth/payment, fall back to existing poll. If pump_fun_graduation_snipe strategy is killed by its own kill_criteria, this consumer becomes orphaned and should be removed.
proposals_for_survival_brain.min_sample_size: N/A — infrastructure work that ENABLES the strategy above. Evaluate via the strategy's metrics.
proposals_for_survival_brain.rollback_plan: Disable the WebSocket consumer; revert to polled pump.fun listener. ~20 LOC removal.
proposals_for_survival_brain.risk_if_wrong: Minimal — additive infrastructure. Worst case: WebSocket flakes and we waste a small amount of CPU on reconnect attempts.
proposals_for_survival_brain.implementation_hint: DEFER until pump_fun_graduation_snipe shadow-validates (proposal above).
